main_issue: Whether and when Agent D can cook strong-smelling fish curry in the shared kitchen without bothering the others' calls, rooms and laundry

A-B.evidence: B said A's 7pm timing doesn't help (T8) and offered a different fix (heads-up). A accepted the Tue/Thu after 7 plan (T19). B never explicitly endorsed the final plan.

A-C.evidence: A wanted no strong-smelling cooking (T1/T5). C said the laundry is affected (T3, T11) and agreed to Tue/Thu (T18). A said Tue/Thu after 7 'works for me' (T19).

A-D.evidence: A softened the ban to weekends or later in the evening (T5). D asked about call times (T6) and proposed Tue/Thu (T17). A confirmed 'Tuesdays and Thursdays after 7' (T19) and D said 'Okay' (T22).

B-C.evidence: Both complained about smell (T2, T3). They never addressed each other. C accepted Tue/Thu (T18). B's close-the-door fix was separate.

B-D.evidence: B asked D to give a heads-up before cooking (T8). D agreed 'I can let you know' (T9). B thanked D (T10).

C-D.evidence: C said the heads-up doesn't help laundry (T11). D asked about timing (T12) and proposed Tue/Thu curry (T17). C said 'that works' (T18).
